# Remember to Die — Skipstone Studios

> Tactical dice combat roguelike with pixel art and dark narrative. Coming September 26th on Steam.

## What is Remember to Die?

Remember to Die is an **indie pixel art roguelike** built by a solo developer in New Zealand. It combines **dice-based tactical combat**, **run-based progression**, and a **dark narrative** about memory and mortality. Think Binding of Isaac meets Balatro — permadeath, build variety, and psychological depth.

It is designed for players who enjoy: roguelikes, roguelites, dice games, turn-based strategy, dungeon crawlers, dark indie games, narrative indie games, and atmospheric pixel art experiences.

## Genre & Tags

- **Roguelike / Roguelite** — permadeath, procedurally generated runs, meta-progression
- **Dice combat** — 32 unique dice, each with distinct tactical abilities
- **Turn-based combat** — strategic, deliberate, no action reflex required
- **Pixel art** — handcrafted pixel art aesthetic with dark atmospheric visuals
- **Indie game** — solo developer, independent studio, no publisher
- **Dungeon crawler** — explore, fight, build your loadout across each run
- **Dark / atmospheric** — themes of death, memory, and mortality
- **Narrative roguelike** — story-driven memory fragment system woven into every run
- **Build variety** — thorns, glass cannon, damage-over-time, self-damage synergies
- **Steam Deck compatible**

## Core Mechanics

**32 Dice** — each with multiple faces and distinct effects. Common, Rare, Relic, and Legendary tiers. Upgrade system: find duplicates to Refine, then Perfect.

**117 Mementos** — items that modify your run. Many carry lore text that callbacks to the narrative fragments you chose, creating a personalised story each run.

**Memory Fragment System** — after each battle, choose a memory fragment marked TRUE or FALSE. Three fragments combine into a Core Memory at chapter's end. Pure (all true), Corrupt (all false), Broken, and Tainted cores each carry different buffs and narrative implications.

**Age Economy** — you don't have HP in the traditional sense. You have a lifespan. Taking fragments costs years. Dying in combat costs years. Managing your age across a run is core to survival.

**Watches** — rare items that modify your starting lifespan and core stats, enabling entirely different build strategies.

## About the Developer

**Skipstone Studios** — solo indie dev studio, New Zealand.

Remember to Die was made by one person over 18 months, mostly between 11pm and 3am. The developer is a 40-something with a 40-year-old dream of making games. No publisher, no team, no budget. Built with Godot, Aseprite, AI tools for base assets, and an obsessive attention to mechanical balance verified via Monte Carlo simulation.

Four previous games (Geneheart, Fa(r)ther, Fox Three, Scorched Earth) are free to play at skipstone.co.nz — each one was deliberate practice before this.
